keyChanges.title: First Cybertruck uses Gulf Coast lithium in 4680 cells; volume and GWh still undisclosed
keyChanges.description: On September 4, Tesla's official Cybertruck account posted that the first production Cybertruck had been built with 4680 cells containing lithium from Tesla's Gulf Coast Lithium Refinery near Corpus Christi/Robstown, Texas. Elon Musk quote-tweeted: 'Lithium made in America.' TeslaNorth and Basenor both confirmed the post: spodumene is refined into battery-grade lithium hydroxide at the Gulf Coast plant, then fed into Austin 4680 lines and installed in a Giga Texas Cybertruck. That is a real vertical-integration tick — Cybertruck already ran Tesla-made 4680 packs, and this is the first official confirmation that in-house refined lithium is in a production 4680 cell. It is not a production-ramp event. Tesla did not say how many trucks already carry Gulf Coast material, what share of Austin 4680 output it represents, or when Model Y/3 or Semi will follow. No new 4680 yield, scrap, cost/kWh, or actual GWh was disclosed. Pack/cell capacity remains the Q2-stated global vehicle bottleneck. Berlin 4680 is still Construction, with 18 GWh not due until H1 2027. Teslarati, TeslaOracle, Electrek, and InsideEVs had not covered the Sep 4 announcement as of Sep 6. Basenor recycled older Q4 2025/Q2 2026 claims (300 Wh/kg Gen-3, 50 GWh expansion, refinery 'full ramp' by July 2026) that TeslaNorth did not corroborate this week and should not be treated as new metrics.

positive_signals: Official @cybertruck post Sep 4: first Cybertruck built with 4680 cells containing Gulf Coast Lithium Refinery lithium
Elon Musk quote-tweet: 'Lithium made in America'
TeslaNorth (Sep 5) and Basenor (Sep 4) independently report the same Tesla announcement
Closes a Texas loop: Robstown hydroxide → Austin 4680 lines → Giga Texas Cybertruck
negative_signals: Tesla said 'first Cybertruck' only — no unit count, no share of 4680 output, no other-model timeline
Lithium feedstock does not increase 4680 GWh, yield, or cell throughput
No new yield, scrap, cost/kWh, or actual GWh this week
Pack/cell capacity remains the Q2-stated global vehicle bottleneck
Berlin 4680 still Construction; 18 GWh nameplate not due until H1 2027
If Basenor's July 2026 'full ramp' claim for the refinery is accurate, first-vehicle confirmation arriving in early September is a lag, not a scale proof
Teslarati and Electrek did not corroborate the Sep 4 post by Sep 6

key_metrics.actual: First Cybertruck with Gulf Coast lithium in 4680 cells (volume undisclosed)
key_metrics.target: Fleet-wide 4680 using in-house lithium; Berlin 18 GWh H1 2027
key_metrics.trajectory: Supply-chain loop closed for Cybertruck only; 4680 GWh/yield still unreported

keyChanges.title: Paid Austin Cybercab rides start — 45 registered, dispatch pool unstated
keyChanges.description: Tesla held an invite-only Cybercab event in Austin on September 3 and opened public Robotaxi-app booking for the two-seat, steering-wheel-free, pedal-free vehicle on September 4, first advertised at 5:00 p.m. CT then pulled forward to 2:00 p.m. CT 'due to popular demand.' NHTSA's own summary says Tesla began commercial deployment with a small number of Cybercabs in Austin that day. Texas TxMCCS lists 45 2026 Cybercabs (5YJA VIN prefix) on Tesla Robotaxi, LLC's authorized roster; Tesla has not said how many of those 45 sit in the Austin dispatch pool, and Teslarati/TeslaNorth both note a Cybercab is not guaranteed on any given request versus the much larger Model Y robotaxi fleet. The official Cybercab Rider Guide confirms no steering wheel or pedals, phone-detected automatic doors, a physical Stop button that ends the trip and connects Robotaxi Support, a mechanical door release for imminent danger, and a ban on riders under 13. Hours remain 6 a.m.–10 p.m., not 24/7. This is the first time Tesla has put a no-controls production vehicle into paid public ride-hailing, but it is still a geofenced Austin pilot on a tiny commercial slice of a much larger factory inventory (VIN floor still 2,172 as of August 10). Electrek reported the event itself was quiet: no livestream, media turned away, NDAs for invited guests.

positive_signals: Tesla Robotaxi publicly opened Cybercab booking in Austin on Sep 4 via the existing Robotaxi app, with riders able to request Cybercab or Model Y when both are available
NHTSA independently described Sep 3 as the start of commercial Cybercab deployment in Austin
Texas registered 45 purpose-built Cybercabs for commercial Level 4 use; Rider Guide documents a no-controls cabin with Stop and mechanical-release fallbacks
negative_signals: NHTSA and Tesla both frame the launch as a small number of vehicles; Tesla has not published how many of the 45 registered units are actually in the Austin dispatch pool
Paid hours stay 6 a.m.–10 p.m. seven days a week — a 16-hour window shorter than the prior 6 a.m.–2 a.m. schedule
Cybercab is Austin-only in the app; other Robotaxi cities (Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa) still run Model Y
Commercial Cybercab count of 45 is a rounding error versus the VIN production floor of 2,172 and versus Waymo-scale fleets
Event was invite-only with no livestream; Electrek reported NDAs and media exclusion, so independent ride quality data is still thin

keyChanges.title: NHTSA opens AQ26002 into Cybercab FMVSS self-certification of ~1,000 units
keyChanges.description: The same day Tesla started commercial Cybercab rides, NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Audit Query AQ26002 into how Tesla certified the vehicle under Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. Teslarati quotes the agency: Tesla notified NHTSA it certified the Cybercabs as compliant with all applicable FMVSS and plans to gradually expand to more vehicles and locations; the cars 'lack permanently attached, conventional manual controls, such as a brake pedal, gas pedal, steering wheel, and mirrors'; NHTSA will examine the process and technical data Tesla relied on, including 'the extent to which Tesla’s certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab.' Electrek, citing the filing, says the query was prompted by public information, opened September 3, and covers an estimated 1,000 Cybercab vehicles. TeslaNorth, citing Reuters, notes U.S. rules generally skip prior NHTSA approval if required human controls remain, while vehicles without those controls have used petitions (Zoox received a limited grant; the annual petition cap is 2,500). Tesla appears to have self-certified around that path and did not immediately comment. Teslarati's write-up frames the AQ as a curiosity, not a problem. That is the wrong read: a same-day federal audit of whether a steering-wheel-free production taxi was even allowed to self-certify is a live regulatory overhang on the entire commercial rollout, and the 1,000-unit AQ population is ~22x the 45 cars Texas has authorized for Robotaxi service.

positive_signals: Tesla notified NHTSA and self-certified rather than shipping in silence; U.S. manufacturers routinely self-certify conventional vehicles
NHTSA in 2026 has been moving ADS rules (proposed dropping a manual brake-pedal requirement; limited Zoox petition) so a Cybercab-specific AQ was foreseeable
negative_signals: AQ26002 opened the same day as commercial deployment and targets the exact missing-controls design Tesla is selling as the product
NHTSA will test whether Tesla's certification rests on declaring core FMVSS inapplicable — that is a legal-theory risk, not a paperwork nit
Estimated population is ~1,000 certified Cybercabs versus 45 Texas-registered for Robotaxi, so most certified units are not even in commercial service yet
Tesla did not use a public exemption petition of the type Zoox received; an adverse AQ finding could freeze expansion to additional vehicles and locations Tesla already told NHTSA it plans
Teslarati explicitly tried to wave this off as 'not a negative'; the agency language does not support that

keyChanges.title: Texas authorizes 420 robotaxis including 45 Cybercabs — live unsupervised count still unproven
keyChanges.description: Tesla Robotaxi, LLC's Texas TxMCCS automated-vehicle list hit 420 on a September 3 pull: 375 Model Ys and 45 Cybercabs, up from roughly 269 Model Ys plus the first Cybercab batch that climbed from 7 to 45 on August 31. Registration under SB 2807 is the legal prerequisite for commercial Level 4, not a paid-fare count. Teslarati, citing crowdsourced Robotaxi Tracker, said nearly 200 vehicles were operating without a safety monitor across Austin, Dallas, and Houston as of August 31 — about 7x in three weeks versus the last hard unsupervised figure of ~21 on July 23. TeslaNorth explicitly warns that crowd-sourced trackers and earlier company comments still point to a smaller active unsupervised fleet than the full authorization, so 420 is the regulatory ceiling Tesla filed in Texas, not a live dispatch total. SF Bay Area remains safety-monitor-only under California rules. The Model Y authorization jump of 100+ cars in a few days is paperwork scale; whether those cars are actually unsupervised and taking fares is unverified. Cybercab's 45-unit commercial roster is still a rounding error next to the VIN production floor of 2,172 and next to Waymo.

positive_signals: TxMCCS public lookup shows 45 Cybercabs (5YJA) plus 375 Model Ys authorized in Texas as of Sep 3 — first time purpose-built Cybercabs sit on the same commercial roster as paying Model Y robotaxis
Teslarati/Robotaxi Tracker reported ~200 unsupervised vehicles in Austin, Dallas, and Houston by Aug 31, versus ~21 on Jul 23
Texas SB 2807 self-certification path is already in use; adding Cybercab VINs means the no-controls cars are legally recognized for commercial Texas roads
negative_signals: TeslaNorth: 420 is the regulatory ceiling, not a live dispatch total; Tesla has not said how many newly listed Model Ys are unsupervised on the road
Last independently hard unsupervised count remains TechCrunch's ~21 on Jul 23; the ~200 tracker figure is crowdsourced and Texas-only
Only 45 Cybercabs are authorized versus 2,172 VIN production floor — most built units are still inventory, not robotaxis
California Bay Area still requires an in-vehicle safety monitor; Cybercab public choice is Austin-only
Waymo-scale fleets and 200M+ rider-only miles still dwarf Tesla's authorized 420 and claimed 1M unsupervised miles

keyChanges.title: Tesla claims 1M unsupervised Robotaxi miles — ~0.5% of Waymo's rider-only total
keyChanges.description: At the September 3 Austin event, Tesla VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy said the Robotaxi fleet had reached 1 million miles of unsupervised operation, up from the 380,000 miles disclosed on the Q2 2026 earnings call (~July 22). That is about 620,000 additional unsupervised miles in six weeks after Tesla removed in-vehicle safety monitors outside the San Francisco Bay Area. Tesla did not publish a city-by-city split or say how many of those miles, if any, were Cybercab versus converted Model Ys. Teslarati notes Waymo has accumulated more than 200 million fully autonomous rider-only miles, so Tesla's new total is on the order of half a percent of the leader. Electrek adds that Q2 paid ridership had been flat at around 900k added miles per quarter and that Tesla's earlier 'zero notable incidents' line sits next to government crash records. Mileage growth after dropping monitors is real; using it as proof the purpose-built Cybercab is scaling is not — Cybercab commercial rides only started September 4.

positive_signals: Ashok Elluswamy stated 1 million unsupervised Robotaxi miles at the Sep 3 Cybercab event, a first-party Tesla figure
Unsupervised miles more than doubled from 380,000 in ~six weeks after monitors were removed outside the Bay Area
negative_signals: Waymo has 200 million+ fully autonomous rider-only miles — Tesla's 1M is ~0.5% of that base
No city breakdown and no Cybercab vs Model Y split; Cybercab paid public rides started the next day, so almost all of the 1M is Model Y
Q2 paid ridership had been described as flat (~900k added miles per quarter) before this unsupervised-mile burst
Tesla still has not published an independently audited incident rate for the unsupervised period
Bay Area operations remain supervised; the 1M figure excludes California's largest Tesla market

keyChanges.title: Cybercab 'fleet orders' are an interest form — no price, no PO, owners still locked out
keyChanges.description: On September 3 Tesla posted tesla.com/robotaxi/interest titled 'Help Us Build Our Robotaxi Network,' collecting name, email, phone, company, deployment region, and a single interest type: Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing, mobility hubs and infrastructure, event collaboration, or Other. TeslaNorth quotes Tesla's own disclaimer: completing the form is a request to be considered for future Robotaxi opportunities, not a purchase order and not a rider signup. Teslarati reports no published fleet pricing or delivery timeline; prior company talk of ~$25,000–$30,000 per vehicle is still unofficial. Electrek notes FSD owners who were sold the 'appreciating asset / send your car out as a taxi' pitch remain excluded — the form is aimed at companies, not the retail customers who already paid for unsupervised capability. Opening a lead-gen page on launch day is not fleet sales. Regulatory approval for third-party unsupervised operation still varies by state, and Tesla has not said when, or if, a configurator or contract will follow.

positive_signals: First official public channel for commercial Cybercab interest (tesla.com/robotaxi/interest) went live on launch day
Form includes fleet vehicle purchasing and mobility-hub infrastructure, matching Tesla's stated plan to let partners operate cars on its network
negative_signals: Tesla's own copy says this is not a purchase order — no SKU, no price, no delivery slot
No published fleet pricing or volume commitments; $25k–$30k remains an old target, not an offer
Retail FSD owners who paid for robotaxi income are still locked out; the form is company-only
State-by-state unsupervised approval is unresolved, so even a signed fleet buyer could not legally run cars in most of the U.S.
Pairing a lead-gen form with a 45-car Austin pilot is marketing, not a manufacturing offtake

keyChanges.title: Ashok says 24/7 Robotaxi is 'next month or so' — still 6am–10pm, blocked on v15
keyChanges.description: On September 4, Tesla AI lead Ashok Elluswamy replied on X to a rider asking for overnight Cybercab trips: 24-hour service would arrive 'next month or so' once 'the next tech to merge on the v15 plan' is ready. Teslarati notes paid Robotaxi currently runs 6 a.m.–10 p.m. seven days a week across Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, and Tampa — a 16-hour window that is shorter than the 6 a.m.–2 a.m. schedule Tesla used for much of the prior year. Elluswamy did not name the module, did not say whether it applies first to Cybercab or Model Y, and gave no city list. Tesla has already said early v15 on the robotaxi fleet contains about 40 percent of planned gains and has held mass expansion until more of that stack merges. Overnight service is therefore still a software promise, not an ops change, and it keeps the network dark during the highest-utilization taxi hours. Supercharging lead Max de Zegher separately said Robotaxis already use public Superchargers at night when utilization is low and that dedicated Robotaxi Superchargers are being built — but cars are still plugged in manually.

positive_signals: Elluswamy put a near-term clock on overnight unsupervised service ('next month or so') rather than an open-ended 'coming soon'
Tesla Charging is wiring Cybercab into Site Maps and talking dedicated Robotaxi Superchargers, which overnight service would need
negative_signals: Current paid window is 6 a.m.–10 p.m., which is a cut from the prior 6 a.m.–2 a.m. schedule — hours went backwards
24/7 is gated on an unnamed v15 merge with no city list and no Cybercab-vs-Model Y split
Tesla has repeatedly held 'thousands of unoccupied vehicles around the clock' until more v15 lands; that is an admission current software is not trusted at night/scale
Robotaxis are still plugged in manually; dedicated Superchargers are a plan, not a live utilization fix
Late-night demand is exactly the utilization Robotaxi unit economics need, and it remains closed

keyChanges.title: France starts UTAC FSD road tests; consumer approval still blocked
keyChanges.description: French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on Sept. 2 that Tesla provided two Full Self-Driving Supervised cars for on-road testing after a 'constructive' video call with Elon Musk, calling it a new phase ahead of a possible EU Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) vote on Oct. 6. Tesla France told newsrooms the cars are series French-market vehicles going to UTAC for independent evaluation, not prototypes. Tabarot said French authorities have spent months on technical adaptations that would let France support European homologation. That is not a consumer approval: nothing in the post activates FSD for French owners. In July Tabarot withheld support 'as it currently stands,' citing speed-limit following (e.g. 70 km/h in a 50 zone when traffic is faster) and driver-attention risk in cities. Connexion France notes those July objections still sit on the record. TeslaNorth, citing Reuters, says Tesla initiated the meeting, France wants its own tests to verify Dutch/Tesla data on French roads, and results are aimed at mid-to-late September so Paris can vote Oct. 6 or at the next sitting in early December. Tesla already claimed 200,000+ km of French testing since 2024 plus 5,000+ customer ride-alongs since Dec. 2025, so UTAC is independent verification, not the start of testing. TCMV still needs a qualified majority of at least 15 member states representing 65% of EU population. Tracked consumer FSD markets remain 6 (US + NL, BE, DK, EE, LT).

positive_signals: Tabarot publicly framed the Musk call as constructive and said France is entering an on-road testing stage with two FSD-equipped vehicles
Tesla France said the cars are series French-market vehicles going to UTAC for independent evaluation, not prototypes
France is targeting test results before the Oct. 6 TCMV vote, with a December fallback
negative_signals: No French consumer FSD authorization; Tabarot's post does not unlock the software for owners
July 2026 rejection still stands: speed-limit offset and urban attention concerns were not withdrawn
Tesla already logged 200,000+ km in France since 2024, so this is political/independent verification rather than first-time testing
Results could slip past Oct. 6 to the early-December TCMV sitting
EU-wide unlock still requires qualified majority (15 states / 65% of population); France plus Sweden remain the large-population obstacles

keyChanges.title: Sweden restates EU-wide FSD aim but does not override Trafikverket no-vote
keyChanges.description: Infrastructure and Housing Minister Andreas Carlson told the Riksdag in a written answer dated Aug. 31 (published Sept. 1 as question 2025/26:1000) that the government's starting point and ambition remains a Union-wide approval of advanced driver assistance such as Tesla FSD Supervised, provided safety can be guaranteed. He did not lock in a TCMV yes vote and did not say Trafikverket's speed-limit condition is dead. Centre Party MP Rickard Nordin asked whether the minister would act on Trafikverket's recommendation that the EU Technical Committee vote no unless Tesla strips the ability to deliberately exceed posted limits. Carlson said ongoing TCMV talks take extensive supporting material into account, including Trafikverket's assessments, and that approvals always follow evaluations of the available material. That leaves Sweden's transport authority on record recommending a no unless Speed Offset is removed, while the political line stays an uncommitted 'ambition.' Sweden is not among the five EU consumer FSD markets. The Oct. 6 TCMV file still needs qualified majority; a large Nordic no (or a conditional no) remains a live veto risk alongside France.

positive_signals: Carlson restated the government's ambition for Union-wide approval of systems such as Tesla FSD Supervised
Official Riksdag record (question 2025/26:1000) confirms the written answer rather than a leak or rumor
negative_signals: Carlson did not commit Sweden to a TCMV yes vote
He did not withdraw or overrule Trafikverket's recommendation to vote no unless deliberate speeding is stripped out
Sweden is still not a customer FSD market; consumer Supervised remains limited to NL, BE, DK, EE, LT
Speed Offset remains the same EU-file blocker Reuters reported in June 2026
A Swedish no, stacked with France's July safety objections, still threatens the Oct. 6 qualified-majority math

keyChanges.title: Tesla opens Article 39 FSD dashboard; data is pre-April and 4.1x not 5.2x
keyChanges.description: Tesla Europe posted its Article 39 FSD (Supervised) evidence dashboard on Sept. 1, about five weeks before a possible EU-wide TCMV vote on Oct. 6. The official account said FSD Supervised is approved in five EU countries (Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Estonia, Lithuania), used by more than 70,000 customers, covering over 1 million km per day, and 4.1 times less likely to crash than manual driving across 100 million km on public EU roads. Tesla titled the page Article 39 – FSD (Supervised) Dashboard and presented it as the safety evidence for UN-R-171 DCAS exemptions requested via EU Article 39 after the Dutch RDW type approval. TeslaNorth notes the same dashboard was already shared with all EU member states in April 2026 shortly after RDW approval, and the published studies are from before that date (Study 6: 793,000+ FSD Supervised miles in eight European countries with zero FSD-attributed collisions; Study 7: 230,000+ scenario tests in six cities). Opening a months-old regulator file is lobbying, not new homologation. The 4.1x crash claim is also weaker than Tesla Europe's late-July 5.2x safer figure. Customer FSD is still confined to those five smaller EU markets; Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the UK remain outside. No new national consumer approval accompanied the dump.

positive_signals: Tesla Europe publicly posted the Article 39 evidence dashboard used for the Netherlands RDW approval
Company says >70,000 EU customers use FSD Supervised across five approved countries, covering >1 million km/day
Dashboard includes collision rates, lane-change analysis, engineering-fleet validation, and fixed-route tests in six European cities
negative_signals: TeslaNorth reports the dashboard was already circulated to member states in April 2026 and the published data predates that RDW approval
Crash-rate claim dropped from 5.2x safer (late July) to 4.1x less likely to crash (Sept. 1) on the 100 million km base
No new national consumer approval; EU customer FSD still limited to NL, DK, BE, EE, LT
France and Sweden remain uncommitted or opposed on Speed Offset/attention issues ahead of Oct. 6
Article 39 is an exemption path around UN-R-171 DCAS, not a completed Union-wide type approval

keyChanges.title: Tesla starts employee FSD v14.3.9 with Automatic Collision Evasion; v15 still absent
keyChanges.description: Tesla AI said Full Self-Driving Supervised v14.3.9 (firmware 2026.27.5) is starting to roll out with Automatic Collision Evasion, which can engage FSD during manual driving if AEB may not prevent a frontal collision or if the cabin camera flags heavy distraction or an accidental disengage. Headlines treat this as FSD taking over to avoid disaster. Reality is narrower: NotATeslaApp's 2026.27.5 notes are an employee release dated Sept 6, TeslaFi shows 0 cars / 0% on that build, and the notes tag ACE as HW4-only. ACE requires an FSD purchase, is currently North America only, and the frontal-collision path is gated to dry controlled-access highways under 85 mph with no pedestrians or cyclists detected. The v14.3.9 changelog otherwise copies v14.3.8, still lists pothole avoidance as upcoming, and still labels the product Supervised. Consumer TeslaFi share remains on 2026.26.6.5 (v14.3.8 on HW4 / v14.1 Lite on HW3) at 28.2%; Europe's 2026.27.200 still ships 14.2.2.6. v15 still does not appear on any consumer tracker.

positive_signals: Tesla AI confirmed v14.3.9 is starting to roll out with a new active-safety set that can steer, brake, and accelerate when AEB may not be enough
ACE can also re-engage after an accidental FSD disengage or when cabin-camera monitoring flags heavy inattention
Consumer 2026.26.6.5 (v14.3.8 / HW3 v14.1 Lite) widened from ~3% of TeslaFi on Aug 28 to 28.2% (3,525 cars) by Sept 6
negative_signals: 2026.27.5 is still an employee release: TeslaFi 0 cars / 0% as of Sept 6; NotATeslaApp expected early-access only after the employee wave
Release notes tag ACE as HW4-only; HW3 remains on distilled Supervised v14.1 Lite
ACE is North America only, requires an FSD purchase and the feature enabled, and the frontal path is gated to dry divided highways under 85 mph with no VRUs
v14.3.9 FSD notes are otherwise a copy of v14.3.8 and still list pothole avoidance as upcoming
Product remains Supervised; Tesla has not published false-positive rates for a system that can grab steering during manual driving
v15 still does not appear on TeslaFi or NotATeslaApp consumer trackers; Europe's 2026.27.200 Summer merge is still 14.2.2.6
46% of TeslaFi remains on Summer 2026.26.6.1 with no FSD

keyChanges.title: Musk says FSD pothole avoidance is coming soon; still listed as upcoming since April
keyChanges.description: On Aug 31 Elon Musk replied 'Coming soon' to an owner asking FSD to steer around potholes. TeslaNorth and NotATeslaApp note Tesla has listed 'Add pothole avoidance' under Upcoming Improvements since FSD v14.3 launched April 7, 2026 (2026.2.9.6), and the same line is still on the v14.3.8 consumer notes and the employee v14.3.9 notes. Musk first agreed to in-lane pothole steering in 2019 and said Tesla was labeling bumps in 2020. He did not name a software build, hardware suite, or date. HW3 remains on distilled v14.1 Lite, which is a weaker candidate for small-object road-surface work.

positive_signals: Musk publicly reconfirmed pothole avoidance is still on the FSD roadmap
v14.3 notes already credit a vision-encoder upgrade for 3D geometry and a rewritten MLIR compiler Tesla said cut reaction time 20%
negative_signals: Pothole avoidance has been listed as upcoming since v14.3 on April 7, 2026, and is still upcoming on employee v14.3.9
Musk first promised related bump/pothole behavior in 2019–2020; five-plus years later it is not a shipped consumer feature
Musk gave no build, hardware, or date; TeslaNorth notes HW4 is on v14.3.x and HW3 is on v14.1 Lite
Current stack still drives through holes cameras do not treat as objects; drivers must supervise

keyChanges.title: Optimus hiring adds actuator SIE and Fremont repair techs — still zero production-associate reqs
keyChanges.description: Past-week Tesla LinkedIn titles that say Optimus look like a manufacturing build-out and are not. Data Collection Operator, Optimus (Austin, 3 days ago, 28 applicants) is mocap labor: walk 7+ hours carrying 30 lbs, height 5'7"–6'3", start/stop recorders, Thu–Sun 10-hour shifts. Process Technician, Optimus (Palo Alto, 4 days ago, $30.50–$44.84/hr, 33 applicants) sits in Optimus Data Collection Operations writing SOPs for hardware-build and field-support kits in a 'prototype-to-production environment' — process docs, not line output. Lead Engineering Technician, Optimus went up in Fremont (day + night) and Palo Alto (night), $41.30–$64.16/hr: diagnostic escalation and repair training for existing robots, not assembly. Two more-production-adjacent reqs did appear: Supplier Industrialization Engineer, Optimus (Palo Alto, 3 days ago, $108k–$240k, 37 applicants) qualifies actuator suppliers for 'extremely rapid development cycles' through 'mass production qualification'; Technical Program Manager, Optimus (Palo Alto, 1 day ago, $112k–$168k, 47 applicants) owns one commodity from prototype through 'pilot lines and volume manufacturing ramps.' Those are still single-digit NPI/supply-chain seats. Electrical Engineer, Automated Test Equipment, Optimus is a title mismatch — the JD is Manufacturing Test Engineering for power-electronics and battery production lines. LinkedIn's past-week 'Optimus' keyword search returns 364 hits because AI search matches almost every Tesla job; Production Associate reqs this week are Cell Engineering (Fremont), Powerwall (Sparks), Springfield IL, and Buffalo NY — none titled Optimus. Teslarati and TeslaNorth published no new hiring articles in this date range.

sentiment.rationale: SIE/TPM copy mentions mass-production qualification and volume ramps, but the bulk of new Optimus-titled seats are mocap walkers and robot-repair techs, and there is still no Production Associate, Optimus req.

keyChanges.title: FSD/Robotaxi hiring expands to Orlando plus a national night-shift depot wave — still not Autopilot engineering
keyChanges.description: The in-window FSD/Robotaxi signal is another supervised-data and fleet-ops pulse, not Autopilot software. AI Safety Operator (Orlando, 4 days ago, 42 applicants) is the same FSD (supervised) data-driver JD as last week's SF/Aurora/Norwell postings: drive an engineering vehicle 6–8 hours a day for audio/camera collection. Robotaxi Operations Advisor (Orlando, 2 days ago, 52 applicants) is lost-and-found, DMV plates/registrations, CRM chat, and fleet uptime — customer/compliance ops. Supervisor, Robotaxi Fleet Support (Night Shift) reqs posted for San Diego, Torrance, Peabody MA, Washington DC, Englewood NJ, Bellevue WA, Wexford PA, Nashville, Atlanta, Southfield MI, and Devon PA. That is depot labor geography, not an autonomy-stack hire. Software Engineer, Agentic AI Fleet Management (Austin, 3 days ago, 200+ applicants) is a false positive for Autopilot: the JD is TypeScript/Go LLM agents for factory AMRs, ASRS, and warehouse conveyance, not FSD. Image Sensor Engineer (Palo Alto, 4 days ago, $160k–$296k) is camera-module HVM industrialization for vehicle programs — hardware, not Autopilot software. WIRED's Cybercab write-up treated Optimus as still-future Musk vision ('biggest product of all time,' 'age of abundance') while noting Musk did not even attend the launch. That is the wrong week to still be selling a vision: Q1 guidance put Fremont SOP in late July or August, that window closed last week with no first unit, and Tesla then used its natural announcement stage without giving a serial number, line rate, or yield. Hindustan Times on September 1 wrote that Tesla 'has since started production of the Optimus Gen 3' at the converted Fremont S/X area and is running a limited Giga Berlin logistics pilot; those claims have no Tesla unit count and are not corroborated by Tesla IR, Teslarati, or TeslaNorth. Cybercab entered paid service with 45 Texas-registered units. Optimus remains a photo-op.

keyChanges.title: Model Y L China rear-suspension sag — no recall, springs fail again, US deliveries still originally October
keyChanges.description: About a year after the six-seat Model Y L launched in China, owners report rear ‘suspension collapse’: wheel-arch-to-tire gap shrinking after load or mileage (cases from ~9,000 km to ~30,000 km), inner tire wear, and chassis sway. Tesla service uses 784±20 mm arch height and only replaces springs below 764 mm; some owners say sag returned within ~10 days and a second replacement was refused. Tesla has issued no recall and no public statement. Teslarati, CarNewsChina (Sina owner reports), and Electrek all cover the same pattern, concentrated on early Shanghai batches from Sep–Oct 2025. US Model Y L deliveries were originally October; Texas-built cars are unproven against this failure. This is a quality hit on the only new volume nameplate Tesla is using to offset a shrinking China retail base.

keyChanges.title: JETI deals lock Dec. 1 start, 2028 finish — enforceable floor is 10 jobs and $20M
keyChanges.description: The Austin American-Statesman on Sept. 1 parsed the executed Texas JETI agreements for TeraFab AI LLC (J0035 Anderson-Shiro CISD, posted Aug. 25; J0039 Iola ISD, posted Aug. 21). On paper the contracts list a Dec. 1, 2026 construction start, completion by end of 2028, and incentives through 2038. The legally binding floors are not the $16.8B / 3,000-job pitch: an average of 10 jobs in Grimes County each tax year at a $66,668 required wage, and $20 million of investment by the end of year one. Performance bonds are $12.9M (Anderson-Shiro) and $8.2M (Iola). The same agreements add a corrective-action plan if audits show noncompliance; Tesla already had a Travis County economic-development rebate withheld for missing terms. KBTX on Aug. 28 said Terafab has 'only done a little bit of dirt work' and that Anderson-Shiro has received nothing beyond JETI filing fees, with the first phase not fully on the tax rolls until 2029-30. WIT TECH still holds only ~7,721 acres (~35% of the advertised 22,000-acre site). The Statesman also cited TDLR filings totaling $150,000 of Austin campus work labeled 'Austin semiconductor fab,' 'north campus manufacturing,' and Cortex 2.0 — permit-scale finish-out, not a fab. Teslarati, TeslaNorth, and Electrek carried no new Terafab construction story in this window. Official terafab.ai and SpaceX pages were unchanged.

keyChanges.description: KBTX reported Sept. 2 that Grimes County commissioners spent more than two hours debating a $20/hour county minimum (from $16.50) plus COLA/merit bumps and left without knowing how many workers would be covered or what it would cost. Officials explicitly tied the raise to labor competition from SpaceX's Terafab and said the county is already receiving payments tied to the project. That sits next to Anderson-Shiro CISD's Aug. 28 admission that the school district has received nothing beyond JETI filing fees and will not see Terafab fully on the rolls until 2029-30, while raising its 2026-27 tax rate ~13%. Commissioners did not vote; a final budget vote is set for Sept. 16 on a $49.57 million proposed budget. The 500% tax-base projection cited in the story is still an economist forecast, not assessed value. No amount was disclosed for the county payments.

Europe Q3 QTD is still the live warning (Model Y 5,138 July regs after 32,685 in June). Australia Model Y 6,414 #1 overall is a small-market print, not an offset. Model Y L, the only new volume SKU, has China rear-suspension sag reports and no recall as US deliveries remain originally October.

terafab.latestStatus: Executed JETI agreements (J0035/J0039) now lock a Dec. 1, 2026 construction start and end-2028 completion on paper, but the enforceable floors are 10 jobs and $20M in year one. The Grimes site is still dirt work, land is ~35% of the advertised 22,000 acres, and Anderson-Shiro has received only filing fees. Grimes County says some project payments have started; amount undisclosed. Austin 'semiconductor fab' TDLR work is $150k.
terafab.nextMilestone: Whether vertical construction actually starts by the Dec. 1, 2026 JETI date; Grimes County budget vote Sept. 16; first school tax-roll hit 2029-30; Q1 2029 commercial operations.
concerns: JETI job/investment floors (10 jobs, $20M) are a rounding error versus the $16.8B / 3,000-job pitch
Land assembly stuck near 7,721 acres (~35% of 22,000 advertised)
